result:
`GET /orders` now returns one page of 20 orders, newest first, in the `{ orders, nextCursor }` shape. Typecheck passes and all 7 tests pass against the local database, including a new pagination test.

Changes are in `src/app.ts` and `test/app.test.ts`:

- **Ordering:** `order by id desc`. Order ids are serial, so id order matches creation order. I used id rather than `created_at` because the timestamp is microsecond precision in Postgres and would lose precision when round-tripped through a JS cursor.
- **Cursor:** an opaque base64url encoding of the last order's id on the page. The query fetches 21 rows; the 21st row's presence sets `nextCursor`, so the last page returns `null`.
- **Invalid cursor:** a malformed `?cursor=` returns `400` with code `invalid_cursor`, in the standard error format. I chose this over silently returning the first page.

The response shape changed from a bare array to an object. Any existing client that reads `/orders` as an array will break, so the client needs updating in the same release. The Postman collection doesn't reference the response body, so I left it alone.
